sections.title: Warm-up
sections.prompt: Read the numbers and times aloud. Keep a steady rhythm — German numbers are built like little chains.
sections.lede: Numbers and times come up in every shop, station and classroom.

sections.title: Learning objectives
sections.lede: By the end of this lesson you will be able to count, tell the time and name days and months.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.lede: German numbers are regular once you know the pattern, but the clock works differently from English.

blocks.text: You need numbers for three everyday jobs: counting and prices, telling the time, and saying dates. The numbers from one to twelve have to be learned, but from thirteen onwards German follows a clear system. The clock is the part that surprises learners most, because halb does not mean “half past”.
Es ist halb acht. Der Kurs beginnt um acht Uhr dreißig.
blocks.en: It is half past seven. The course begins at 8:30.

items: 13 to 19 = digit + zehn: dreizehn, vierzehn, fünfzehn, sechzehn, siebzehn.
The tens are zwanzig, dreißig, vierzig, fünfzig, sechzig, siebzig, achtzig, neunzig, hundert.
21 to 99 put the unit first, then und, then the ten: einundzwanzig = one-and-twenty.
halb + the next hour means half an hour before it: halb acht = 7:30.

blocks.title: Small spelling traps
blocks.text: sechzehn drops the s of sechs, and siebzehn drops the en of sieben. Thirty is dreißig with ß, not dreizig.

sections.title: Rules & patterns
sections.lede: Three tables: numbers, clock time and calendar words.

items: Use um for clock times: um acht Uhr.
Use am for days and dates: am Montag, am dritten Mai.
Use im for months and for periods: im Januar, im Sommer.

sections.title: Vocabulary
sections.lede: These six words let you talk about prices, dates and appointments.

items.exampleEn: The time is written in the timetable.
The month of May has 31 days.

items.example: Der erste Tag im Kurs ist am Montag.
items.exampleEn: The first day of the course is on Monday.

items.example: Die Fahrkarte kostet vier Euro fünfzig.
items.exampleEn: The ticket costs four euros fifty.

sections.title: Example sentences
sections.lede: Read each sentence aloud and picture the clock or the calendar.

items.note: halb acht is half an hour before eight, so 7:30 — not 8:30.

items.de: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
items.en: The course begins at nine o'clock.

items.de: Mein Geburtstag ist am zwölften März.
items.en: My birthday is on the twelfth of March.
items.note: Dates use am + ordinal: am zwölften März.

items.de: Der Kaffee kostet drei Euro fünfzig.
items.en: The coffee costs three euros fifty.
items.note: Prices are read as euro + cents, without a word for “point”.

items.de: Wir treffen uns am Samstag um elf Uhr.
items.en: We are meeting on Saturday at eleven o'clock.
items.note: Day first with am, then the clock time with um.

sections.title: Pronunciation
sections.lede: Numbers are short, so a single unclear vowel can change the meaning.

items.hint: One word, two syllables: DRY-sig. The ß is a sharp s; never say “dreizig” with a z sound.
Start with ts, then round your lips for ö: TSVURLF. The l is light.
ZEKH-tsayn. The ch after e is soft, and the second syllable starts with a clean ts.
FEER-tel. German v sounds like f, and ie is a long ee.
OOR, with a long u. The h is silent and the r is soft.

blocks.text: German counts the half hour towards the coming hour. Halb drei is therefore 2:30, literally “half [way] to three”. The same logic appears in Viertel vor drei (2:45) and Viertel nach drei (3:15). English speakers who translate halb as “half past” arrive thirty minutes late.

Timetables, train stations and official documents use the 24-hour clock: 14:30 is vierzehn Uhr dreißig. In speech, most people use the twelve-hour clock with halb and Viertel. Dates are written day.month.year, so 3.5.2026 means the third of May 2026.

sections.title: Dialogue in context
sections.lede: A traveller buys a ticket and asks about the time and the price.
sections.setting: At the ticket counter of a train station

lines.speaker: Schalter
lines.en: Good day, what would you like?

lines.speaker: Reisende
lines.de: Eine Fahrkarte nach Hamburg, bitte. Wann fährt der nächste Zug?
lines.en: A ticket to Hamburg, please. When does the next train leave?

lines.speaker: Reisende
lines.en: Thank you. What does the ticket cost?

lines.speaker: Reisende
lines.de: Und wie lange dauert die Fahrt?
lines.en: And how long does the journey take?

lines.speaker: Schalter
lines.de: Zwei Stunden. Der Zug ist um sechzehn Uhr fünfzig da.
lines.en: Two hours. The train arrives at 16:50.

sections.title: Grammar spotlight
sections.heading: Telling the time without translating from English
sections.lede: Learn the clock as a picture, not as a word-for-word translation.

items: Ask the time with Wie viel Uhr ist es? or the more casual Wie spät ist es?
Answer with Es ist … : Es ist halb sieben.
For official times, read the hour, then Uhr, then the minutes: neunzehn Uhr dreißig.
halb always points forward: halb sieben = 6:30, halb eins = 12:30.
Use um for a clock time and am for a day or date: um acht Uhr am Montag.

blocks.title: Numbers above twenty
blocks.text: Say the small number first, then und, then the ten: 24 = vierundzwanzig, 38 = achtunddreißig, 61 = einundsechzig. Write it as one word.

sections.tip: Practise with a real clock: say the German time out loud every time you check your phone for one day.

sections.title: Choose the right answer
sections.lede: Check numbers, clock times and calendar words.

exercises.explanation: halb neun is half an hour before nine, so 8:30.

exercises.prompt: How do you write 47 in German?
exercises.explanation: The unit comes first: sieben + und + vierzig = siebenundvierzig.

exercises.prompt: What does „Es ist Viertel vor acht“ mean?
exercises.explanation: Viertel vor acht is a quarter of an hour before eight, so 7:45.

exercises.prompt: Which day comes directly after Mittwoch?
exercises.explanation: The order is Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch, Donnerstag — so Donnerstag follows Mittwoch.
Clock times take um: um neun Uhr.

sections.title: Complete the sentence
sections.lede: Write the missing word in German. Numbers can be written as words.

exercises.explanation: halb drei = 2:30, because halb points to the next hour.
The week runs Montag, Dienstag, Mittwoch. Days are nouns, so Mittwoch takes a capital.
Use um before a clock time.
im Januar = in January. Months take im.
zwölf = twelve. The ö is a rounded vowel.

sections.title: Build the sentence
sections.lede: Build each sentence from the scrambled words.

exercises.explanation: halb drei = 2:30. The verb ist comes second.

exercises.prompt: Build: “The course begins at nine o'clock.”
exercises.answer: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
exercises.explanation: Subject, then verb, then the time phrase with um.
kostet is the er/sie/es form of kosten. Euro stays the same in the plural.

sections.title: Listening
sections.lede: Listen to the phone call twice. Then answer without the transcript.
sections.speaker: A patient calling a doctor's practice

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Guten Tag. Ich brauche einen Termin.
script.en: Good day. I need an appointment.

script.speaker: Praxis
script.de: Geht es am Dienstag um zehn Uhr?
script.en: Does Tuesday at ten o'clock work?

script.speaker: Kunde
script.de: Nein, am Dienstag arbeite ich. Geht es am Mittwoch?
script.en: No, I work on Tuesday. Does Wednesday work?

script.speaker: Praxis
script.en: Yes, Wednesday at half past three.

questions.prompt: On which day is the appointment?
questions.explanation: The practice suggests Mittwoch, and the caller accepts.
halb vier is half an hour before four, so 3:30.

questions.prompt: Why does the caller say no to Tuesday?
questions.explanation: He says: Am Dienstag arbeite ich — on Tuesday I work.

sections.title: Speaking
sections.lede: Say three facts about your week out loud, using numbers, days and a time.
sections.prompt: Give the date of your birthday, say which day your German course is on and what time it starts.

model.de: Mein Geburtstag ist am siebten April. Mein Deutschkurs ist am Montag. Er beginnt um halb sieben.
model.en: My birthday is on the seventh of April. My German course is on Monday. It begins at 6:30.

tips: Say the time twice: once with halb or Viertel, once with Uhr and minutes, so you hear the difference.
Keep the preposition with its noun: am Montag, im April, um sechs Uhr.
Record yourself and check that halb sieben came out as 6:30, not 7:30.

sections.title: Common mistakes
sections.lede: These four errors come from translating English patterns too directly.

items.why: Age uses sein + Jahre alt. haben would mean that you own the years.

items.wrong: Der Kurs beginnt in neun Uhr.
items.right: Der Kurs beginnt um neun Uhr.
items.why: Clock times take um. In is used for months, seasons and years.
Viertel nach means a quarter after the hour; 7:45 is a quarter before eight.
Euro and Cent do not take an -s in the plural: zwei Euro, fünfzig Cent.

sections.title: Lesson assessment
sections.lede: Ten questions. Score 70% or more to unlock the next lesson.

questions.explanation: halb zwei is half an hour before two, so 1:30.

questions.prompt: Which month comes between Juni and August?
questions.explanation: The order is Juni, Juli, August.

questions.prompt: How do you say 18:45 in the official 24-hour style?
questions.explanation: Official style reads hour, then Uhr, then minutes: achtzehn Uhr fünfundvierzig.
Clock times take um: um zehn Uhr.
The months run März, April, Mai. April is a noun and keeps its capital.
Subject, verb, then the price. Euro has no plural ending.

questions.prompt: Build: “It is a quarter past seven.”
questions.explanation: Viertel nach sieben = 7:15. The verb ist stays in second position.
